claim_text: The unusual quarternaty structure of AdhE was noticed very early; 20-60 subunits are helically arranged to form rod-like ultrastructures that appear to change conformation in the presence of Fe 2+ and NADH [ Kessler92 ]. More recently, cryo-EM structures confirmed the higher-order helical architecture and conformational changes upon cofactor addition [ Kim19 , Pony20 , Kim20 ]. The two active sites are topologically separated; ALDH active sites face the outer surface, while ADH active sites face the inner surface [ Kim19 ]. Helical filament formation is essential for AdhE function in vitro and in vivo ; the extended conformation allows substrate channeling between the two active sites [ Pony20 , Kim20 ]. Crystal structures of the apo- and cofactor-bound alcohol dehydrogenase domain of AdhE have been solved at 1.95 and 1.65 Å resolution, respectively [ Azmi20 ]. Using a method that distinguishes N-phosphorylation from O-phosphorylation, N-phosphorylation was detected in vitro [ Hu20 ].

claim_text: AdhE is one of the major proteins damaged by oxidative stress, and its expression is low under aerobic conditions [ Tamarit98 ]. However, AdhE mutants that confer the ability to grow aerobically on ethanol can be selected [ MembrilloHernan00 ]; their in vivo activity depends on protection against metal-catalyzed oxidation by the chaperone DnaK [ Echave02 ]. A Glu568Lys substitution identified in the adhC mutant also confers high activity of the enzyme under aerobic assay conditions [ HollandStaley00 ]. AdhE's aerobic role is uncertain, but it may protect against oxidative stress, acting as a hydrogen peroxide scavenger [ Echave03 ]. Under aerobic conditions, AdhE may be protected against metal-catalyzed oxidation in the presence of copper [ Matuszewska08 ] and heat inactivation [ Matuszewska09 ] by the heat shock proteins IbpA and IbpB.
